narrative.overview: A thin brass line connecting what you typed to what they said. Quiet by default and compact, like brass instrument markings on cold slate. The boldness is spent once, on the swap-back fix.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first brass-on-slate for Readback's own surfaces (popup, options, site). The Gmail overlay follows the host's theme.
One accent, brass, used as a signal: open asks, focus, the primary fix and the readback line. Never for errors.
Slips are red squiggles, always paired with a citation, never with a generic "spelling" label.
Evidence is set in Geist Mono: the cited amount, name or date the guard compared against.
Depth from a cold surface ladder and hairlines. Shadows only on things that float over a host page.
Zero motion on keystrokes. One choreographed moment on the fix.

rules.name: The Brass Means Reading Rule
rules.body: Brass says "Readback is reading this with you": open asks, focus and the fix. It never marks a mistake. Mistakes are red, carry an icon and are always cited.

rules.name: The No Orphan Red Rule
rules.body: A red squiggle never appears without a reachable citation: hover, Alt+Shift+J, or the ledger's slip list. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning.

rules.name: The Five Percent Rule
rules.body: Brass covers ≤ 5% of pixels on any screen, with at most one brass-filled button per view.

rules.name: The Evidence Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets only text quoted from the thread or text that must be read exactly. It never sets decorative labels, eyebrows or headings.

rules.name: The Three Hubots Rule
rules.body: Hubot Sans appears in at most 3 places per screen. In the extension it appears only on the options page title and section titles. The popup and overlay are Mona-only.

rules.name: The No Caps Rule
rules.body: No all-caps labels and no tracked-out eyebrows anywhere. Taxonomy, where real, is sentence case at label size in text-muted.

rules.name: The Guest Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this floats over a page we don't own". Nothing inside our own pages gets a shadow except e4 dialogs.

dos: Do cite the thread in every slip message, in the reader's terms: `She signs Kathryn`, not `Possible misspelling`.
Do set every quoted value in Geist Mono with `tnum`, exactly as the thread wrote it.
Do follow the host's theme in the overlay (measure the editor background luminance) and `prefers-color-scheme` in our own pages, with a System/Light/Dark toggle on the site.
Do keep one brass-filled button per view (the primary fix in the card, Open the playground in the empty popup, Load a sample thread in the empty playground).
Do label every synthetic example `Sample thread`.
Do reserve pill and count widths in `ch` so nothing shifts.
donts: Don't use warning amber or info blue anywhere. Their hues collide with brass or add a second accent.
Don't add a draw-in animation to squiggles, a stagger to ledger rows, or hover lift on anything.
Don't use pills for buttons. The ask pill is the only full-radius element besides switch thumbs.
Don't show a model's guess as a fact: model-derived coverage is always the dotted ring until the user confirms.
Don't place the pill over Gmail's toolbar or Send button, or anywhere a click could be mistaken for sending.
Don't reproduce reference-brand surfaces (no lavender, no red stripes, no white CTA, no indigo hero, no #010102/#07080a ladders), names or proprietary fonts.
